tagline.text: Ayala Center's big shopping mall in Makati, with a rooftop of Korean and Japanese restaurants

location.label: Location
location.text: Ayala Center, Makati City (Palm Drive, near Ayala Avenue)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~3,000 (per person, half day including meals and window-shopping)

children.text: Glorietta is a large shopping complex in the middle of Ayala Center in the Makati Central Business District. Across Glorietta 1 to 5 it has more than 500 stores, cinemas and a rooftop of Korean and Japanese restaurants, and it gets packed from November with big Christmas displays.

Glorietta is a large shopping complex inside Ayala Center, in the Makati Central Business District of Metro Manila. It is run by Ayala Malls, part of the property developer Ayala Land. Glorietta 1, 2, 3 and 4 are connected to one another, while Glorietta 5 stands separately across the street and is linked by a basement walkway. The total floor area is about 250,000 sq m, one of the largest in the Philippines, and there are more than 500 stores. According to Wikipedia, together with Greenbelt, which is of a similar size, it is one of the two big shopping complexes that define Makati.

The story begins with Glorietta Park, laid out in the 1970s. When Ayala Center was redeveloped, the mall opened in 1991 under the name Quad, and it was renamed Glorietta in 1997. Expansions ran from 1999 to 2005, and Glorietta 5 opened in 2008. On October 19, 2007, an explosion in Glorietta 2 killed 11 people. It was first reported as an LPG gas accident at a restaurant and a bomb was also suggested, but Glorietta 2 has since been demolished and rebuilt. Glorietta 1 and 2 were torn down in 2010 and reopened in late 2012, and Holiday Inn & Suites Makati arrived in 2013.

Each section has its own character. Glorietta 1 and 2 have mid-priced and local fashion brands, Glorietta 3 has international luxury brands and restaurants, Glorietta 4 has the cinemas and The Marketplace supermarket, and Glorietta 5 has Uniqlo's flagship store, reportedly among the largest in Southeast Asia, plus a church. The fourth-floor rooftop, Top of the Glo, has Japan Town and K-Park, where Korean and Japanese restaurants cluster. Korean travelers also know it as a place to stop by when they miss Korean food. The layout is complicated and easy to get lost in, so it helps to take a photo of the floor directory at the entrance.

Glorietta is currently in the middle of a major renovation. Ayala Land has been working in phases since 2024, and a new facade, a new logo and more open-air space are being unveiled step by step. Wikipedia says Mettacity opened in February 2026 and that the Troopers food hall in Glorietta 4 closed for renovation in April 2026. In work zones, escalators and walkways are sometimes closed temporarily, so please check the latest announcements before you go. The area is also a stage for modern Makati history. In July 2003, soldiers staged the Oakwood mutiny at the neighboring Oakwood hotel (now the Ascott Makati), and Glorietta was closed during that time. Today it is an ordinary shopping route, but knowing these events makes the complex's history feel more vivid as you walk through. More recently, a huge LED screen of about 300 sq m was unveiled in the Glorietta 4 cinema lobby in mid-2025, and in June 2025 a third-floor bridge linking Glorietta 5 and One Ayala opened, making getting around easier.

More than 500 stores let you browse fashion, cosmetics, accessories and electronics in one go. It connects to Rustan's department store in the same complex, and Glorietta 3 has many international brands and restaurants. It is a good way to spend half a day in the air conditioning on a rainy day.

There is an open-air space on the fourth-floor rooftop of Glorietta 1 and 2, with Japan Town and K-Park. Korean and Japanese restaurants, cafes and bars gather here, and the atmosphere is lovely around sunset. Tenants change often, so check on site.

This event space between Glorietta 1 and 2 hosts pop-up events and performances throughout the year. In November 2012, the Guinness World Record for the most people modeling on a catwalk, with 2,255 participants, was set here (it was surpassed in 2015). You can check the event schedule in Ayala Malls announcements or its app.

Christmas in the Philippines starts in September, and Glorietta usually holds its tree lighting around mid-November. In 2025 the lighting took place on November 15 under the theme "That Holiday Feeling," followed by a huge indoor tree, a gift market and a designer bazaar. The schedule differs every year, so check the announcements.
Glorietta 4 has the cinemas and The Marketplace, a large supermarket that is good for groceries and imported foods. Check the movie schedule in the cinema app or on site.

Second-floor walkways lead to SM Makati and The Landmark, and a third-floor walkway links Glorietta 5 and One Ayala. You can also walk to Greenbelt in the same complex, so a day of visiting several malls is easy. Between the buildings, small green spaces and plazas such as Glorietta Park, Glorietta Plaza and Palm Promenade offer a quick breath of fresh air in the middle of shopping.

blocks.title: Hotels and offices in one complex

children.text: Holiday Inn & Suites Makati and the Ascott Makati hotel connect directly to the mall. The advantage of this complex is that you can shop and eat without getting wet from your room.
At the Glorietta 3 entrance, take a photo of the floor directory, then start with the international brand floors.
Have lunch in the dining area on the Glorietta 1 and 2 side. If you crave Korean food, going up to K-Park on the rooftop is also a good idea.
Buy groceries and souvenirs at The Marketplace in Glorietta 4, and rest for a while at the cinema.
Follow the second-floor walkway to look around SM Makati or The Landmark.
Have dinner on the Top of the Glo rooftop while watching the sunset.
Staying out of the heat and rain keeps the plan on track even in the rainy season. To reach Uniqlo in Glorietta 5, use the basement walkway.
Start with a light walk around Ayala Triangle.
Look around Glorietta and have lunch.
Walk to Greenbelt and rest at a cafe or an outdoor restaurant.
Have dinner at a restaurant in central Makati and take Grab back to your hotel.

items.title: From the Manila airport and city

children.text: From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), a taxi or Grab to Ayala Center in Makati is the easiest option. Travel time varies a lot with traffic, so allow plenty of margin.
From central Manila or Malate, Grab is also convenient. Enter "Glorietta Palm Drive" or "Ayala Center" as the destination.
The Ayala Avenue area is heavily congested during rush hour (weekdays, 5 to 8 p.m.).
Getting off at MRT-3 Ayala Station connects you toward Ayala Center. You can walk from the station to Glorietta, but check the route on site.
The EDSA Busway also has an Ayala stop.

items.title: Bus and getting around the complex

children.text: Buses to destinations around Makati and the BGC Bus (L16) run from the Glorietta bus terminal. Routes can change, so check the local information.
Within the complex you get around on foot, with walkways to Greenbelt, SM Makati and One Ayala.
As an indoor mall, it can be visited year-round. Evenings on weekends and around payday are crowded, so weekday mornings are quieter.
From mid-November through January the Christmas decorations and events make it most spectacular, but also busiest. The rooftop Top of the Glo is nicest on cooler dry-season evenings.

The Holiday Inn & Suites Makati and the Ascott Makati, which are attached to the mall, are the most convenient places to stay. Holiday Inn connects between Glorietta 1 and 2 and the Ascott on the Glorietta 4 side, so you can keep shopping and eating without an umbrella even on rainy days. Makati also has hotels from budget to luxury, so you can choose to suit your budget. Rates vary greatly by season, so compare them on a booking app.

The mall has Filipino, Korean, Japanese and Western food. Glorietta 3 has restaurants such as Hard Rock Cafe, and the rooftop K-Park has Korean restaurants and cafes. At The Marketplace you can buy groceries all in one go.
The layout is as complicated as a maze, so take a photo of the floor directory at the entrance.
The air conditioning is strong, so bring a light jacket.
On weekend evenings in the Christmas season the parking lots and Grab pick-up zones are very crowded. Weekday daytime is recommended.
Some sections are under construction, so certain escalators and walkways may be closed temporarily. If you are headed to a particular shop, ask the information desk for a detour.

Greenbelt, SM Makati and The Landmark are close by, so if you cannot find something in one mall, try another. Since they are in the same complex, you often just cross a street, and many travelers visit two or three in a day.
The Uniqlo in Glorietta 5 is big, with a wide choice of sizes and colors. It is separate from the main building, so checking the basement walkway location beforehand keeps you from getting lost.
When you miss Korean food, head to K-Park on the rooftop, but tenants change often, so check on a map app whether a place is open before you go.
Hours differ by section and shop. Event-venue listings show about 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., but this may be outdated, so check the latest announcement.
It is crowded, so watch for pickpockets and bag theft, and follow the signs around construction zones.
On crowded escalators and in food courts, carry your bag in front and do not leave your phone out.
Take a taxi or Grab only at official pick-up zones, and make sure the meter is used.
Do not go past construction barriers or temporary-route signs.
During typhoon or heavy rain warnings, the mall's operating hours may change, so check announcements.
When it rains, some rooftop restaurant areas may not operate.
A shopping mall in the same Ayala Center, reached on foot. It has outdoor gardens and a dining area, so it pairs well with Glorietta.
It can be combined with other plans exploring the business district and the dining and bar streets.
You can get there by Grab, and the BGC Bus (L16) also runs from the Glorietta bus terminal. Travel time varies greatly with traffic.
